name: ag-ui
description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
readmeExcerpt:
### The open protocol that connects any agent to any app. **[Docs](https://docs.ag-ui.com)** · **[Examples](https://dojo.ag-ui.com)** · **[Spec](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0)** · **[Discord](https://discord.gg/Jd3FzfdJa8)**

**AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.** Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack. > [!IMPORTANT] > **AG-UI 1.0 is here.** The protocol now has a stable, frozen [specification](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0) backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. [What changed →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0/changelog) · [Migration guide →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/migrating-to-1-0) ## Quick start **Start a new app.** The CLI scaffolds a frontend ([CopilotKit](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit) on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick: ```bash npx create-ag-ui-app@latest ``` Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before `npm run dev`: ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..." ```
Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client
An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a `RunAgentInput` and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one. **1. The agent (Python).** Requires Python 3.9+. ```bash pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn ``` ```python # server.py import uuid from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse from ag_ui.core import ( PROTOCOL_VERSION, RunAgentInput, RunStartedEvent, RunFinishedEvent, TextMessageStartEvent, TextMessageContentEvent, TextMessageEndEvent, ) from ag_ui.encoder import EventEncoder app = FastAPI() @app.post("/") async def run_agent(input_data: RunAgentInput, request: Request): encoder = EventEncoder(accept=request.headers.get("accept")) async def events(): yield encoder.encode(RunStartedEvent( thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id, protocol_version=PROTOCOL_VERSION, )) message_id = str(uuid.uuid4()) yield encoder.encode(TextMessageStartEvent(message_id=message_id, role="assistant")) for chunk in ["Hello ", "from ", "AG-UI!"]: yield encoder.encode(TextMessageContentEvent(message_id=message_id, delta=chunk)) yield encoder.encode(TextMessageEndEvent(message_id=message_id)) yield encoder.encode(RunFinishedEvent(thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id)) return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type=encoder.get_content_type()) ``` ```bash uvicorn server:app --port 8000 ``` **2. The client (TypeScript).** In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+. ```bash npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module npm install @ag-ui/client tsx ``` ```ts // client.ts import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client"; const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: "http://localhost:8000/" }); agent.addMessage({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), role: "user", content: "Hi there!" }); await agent.runAgent({}, { onRunStartedEvent: ({ event }) => console.log(`run started (AG-UI ${event.protocolVersion})`), onTextMessageContentEvent: ({ event }) => { process.stdout.write(event.delta); }, onRunFinishedEvent: () => console.log("\nrun finished"), }); ``` ```bash npx tsx client.ts ``` You should see `Hello from AG-UI!` stream in. Swap the server for any [supported framework](#integrations) and the client doesn't change.
## Where AG-UI fits AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. **MCP** gives agents tools and context, **A2A** lets agents work with other agents, and **AG-UI** brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. [Read more →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/agentic-protocols) > [!NOTE] > **AG-UI or A2UI?** They work together. [A2UI](https://github.com/google/A2UI), MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are *generative UI specs*: they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the *runtime protocol* that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. [Learn more →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/concepts/generative-ui-specs) ## Integrations AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the [Dojo](https://dojo.ag-ui.com).

| @ag-ui/langgraph | 0.0.47 | `npm install @ag-ui/langgraph@0.0.47` |

#### @ag-ui/langgraph@0.0.47

- Added a `durability` agent option; the adapter sends it with runs and uses it to read boundary checkpoints instead of a client-controlled `forwardedProps.durability`.
- Client `forwardedProps` now reach `runs.stream` only via an allowlist (`streamSubgraphs`, `durability`); `context`, `checkpoint`, `checkpointId` and others are dropped with a warning.
- `forwardedProps.config` is no longer merged over `assistantConfig`; `forwardedProps.command` accepts only `resume` (`goto`/`update` dropped with a warning).
- Continue mode now resumes only from the node that thread history shows ran in the latest step, using it as `asNode`, and filters client state by the graph input schema.
- A continue that would change an input channel now starts a new run so prior gates re-evaluate the changed input.
- A continue that proceeds unchanged no longer writes client state, avoiding reducer channels (e.g. `operator.add`) doubling stored values.
- Fixed a pending interru

#### @ag-ui/client@1.0.5

- `compactEvents` now preserves message order and snapshot boundaries across overlapping streams, fixing swapped parallel tool calls and deltas overwritten by mid-stream snapshots.
- Events arriving between overlapping streams now keep their arrival order, avoiding `STEP_STARTED`/`STEP_FINISHED` sequences rejected by `verifyEvents`.
- Reasoning message deltas (`REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT`) are now compacted like text messages, greatly reducing stored history size.
- Large replayed threads apply much faster via a `MessageLookup` index replacing full-list scans by message and tool call id.
- `AbstractAgent.clone()` now copies `resolvingPeerCeiling`, so clones retain all own fields.
- Enforcement now rejects missing, non-string, or inherited union discriminators.

##### Breaking changes

readmeHtml:
The open protocol that connects any agent to any app.

Docs · Examples · Spec · Discord


AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

Important

AG-UI 1.0 is here. The protocol now has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. What changed → · Migration guide →

Quick start

Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend (CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick:

npx create-ag-ui-app@latest

Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev:

export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client

An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a RunAgentInput and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one.

1. The agent (Python). Requires Python 3.9+.

pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn
# server.py
import uuid

from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from ag_ui.core import (
    PROTOCOL_VERSION,
    RunAgentInput,
    RunStartedEvent,
    RunFinishedEvent,
    TextMessageStartEvent,
    TextMessageContentEvent,
    TextMessageEndEvent,
)
from ag_ui.encoder import EventEncoder

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/")
async def run_agent(input_data: RunAgentInput, request: Request):
    encoder = EventEncoder(accept=request.headers.get("accept"))

    async def events():
        yield encoder.encode(RunStartedEvent(
            thread_id=input_data.thread_id,
            run_id=input_data.run_id,
            protocol_version=PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        ))
        message_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        yield encoder.encode(TextMessageStartEvent(message_id=message_id, role="assistant"))
        for chunk in ["Hello ", "from ", "AG-UI!"]:
            yield encoder.encode(TextMessageContentEvent(message_id=message_id, delta=chunk))
        yield encoder.encode(TextMessageEndEvent(message_id=message_id))
        yield encoder.encode(RunFinishedEvent(thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id))

    return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type=encoder.get_content_type())
uvicorn server:app --port 8000

2. The client (TypeScript). In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+.

npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module
npm install @ag-ui/client tsx
// client.ts
import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client";

const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: "http://localhost:8000/" });

agent.addMessage({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), role: "user", content: "Hi there!" });

await agent.runAgent({}, {
  onRunStartedEvent: ({ event }) => console.log(`run started (AG-UI ${event.protocolVersion})`),
  onTextMessageContentEvent: ({ event }) => { process.stdout.write(event.delta); },
  onRunFinishedEvent: () => console.log("\nrun finished"),
});
npx tsx client.ts

You should see Hello from AG-UI! stream in. Swap the server for any supported framework and the client doesn't change.

Where AG-UI fits

AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

Note

AG-UI or A2UI? They work together. A2UI, MCP Apps, and Open-JSON-UI are generative UI specs: they describe what UI an agent wants to show. AG-UI is the runtime protocol that carries those payloads, along with everything else, between the agent and the app. Learn more →

Integrations

AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo.

Don't see your framework? Build an integration →

Full list of integrations

Show all integrations
  • Partners: LangChain · CrewAI
  • Built in: Microsoft Agent Framework · Google ADK (JS) · Google Antigravity · AWS Strands Agents · Mastra · Pydantic AI · Agno · LlamaIndex · AG2
  • More frameworks: Claude Agent SDK · Claude Managed Agents · IBM watsonx Orchestrate · Langroid · Spring AI · Cloudflare Agents · Omnara · Genkit (Go) · OpenAI Agents
  • Specs: Oracle Agent Spec
  • Deployment: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

Source for every integration lives in integrations/ and middlewares/, and the demos in apps/dojo.

SDKs

Language Install Reference
TypeScript npm install @ag-ui/client Docs · Source
Python pip install ag-ui-protocol Docs · Source
.NET dotnet add package AGUI.Client Docs · Source

Community SDKs: Kotlin · Go · Java · Dart · Rust · Ruby · C++ · Swift

Features: what you can build

Each building block maps to events in the spec, and each has a live demo in the AG-UI Dojo.

Building block What it does Try it
Streaming chat Token-by-token messages across multi-turn sessions, with cancel and resume Demo
Generative UI Agents render typed components, or declarative UI with A2UI and MCP Apps Demo
Shared state A typed store the agent and app both read and write, synced with snapshots and JSON Patch deltas Demo
Frontend tools The agent calls tools that run in the app, and gets the result back Demo
Human in the loop Runs end with an interrupt outcome; the user approves, edits, or rejects, and the next run resumes Demo
Reasoning Show the agent's reasoning as it works, including encrypted reasoning round-trips Demo
Subagents Nested delegation, with every event attributed to the subagent run that produced it Demo
Multimodal Images, audio, video, and documents in user input and tool results Demo

Tool output streaming, backend tool rendering, activity progress, token usage, and custom events are covered in the docs. Here's a quick tour of the Dojo:

dojo.mp4

How it works

Your app starts a run by sending the agent a single RunAgentInput: the conversation, the tools the frontend offers, shared state, and context. The agent answers with a stream of typed events from eight families: run lifecycle, text messages, tool calls, state, reasoning, activity, subagents, and custom events (full list). Only the run lifecycle is required, so a minimal agent emits a handful of events and grows from there.

AG-UI is transport-agnostic. The spec defines HTTP + SSE and a binary HTTP + Protobuf binding, and middleware can adapt events from any source. Read the architecture overview for the full picture.

Event reference

AG-UI 1.0 defines 31 event types in eight families. See the spec for every field.

Event family Events
Runs and steps RUN_STARTED RUN_FINISHED RUN_ERROR STEP_STARTED STEP_FINISHED
Text messages TEXT_MESSAGE_START TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT TEXT_MESSAGE_END TEXT_MESSAGE_CHUNK
Tool calls TOOL_CALL_START TOOL_CALL_ARGS TOOL_CALL_END TOOL_CALL_RESULT TOOL_CALL_CHUNK
State STATE_SNAPSHOT STATE_DELTA (JSON Patch) MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT
Reasoning REASONING_START REASONING_MESSAGE_* REASONING_ENCRYPTED_VALUE REASONING_END
Activity ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT ACTIVITY_DELTA
Subagents SUBAGENT_STARTED SUBAGENT_FINISHED SUBAGENT_ERROR
Passthrough RAW CUSTOM

Community

  • Questions and ideas: Discord and GitHub Discussions
  • Bugs: GitHub Issues
  • What's next: the roadmap and the draft spec

Contributing

Contributions are welcome: new integrations, SDKs, docs, and fixes. Start with CONTRIBUTING.md, and use the server starter and middleware starter as templates for new integrations. Report security issues as described in SECURITY.md.

AG-UI was created by CopilotKit and is developed in the open with the community.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Event‑based protocol that standardizes real‑time AI agent interaction with user interfaces
aiSummary.whatItDoes: AG-UI solves the lack of a common contract for streaming agent events to front‑end applications. It defines ~16 standard event types and a minimal set of inputs that agent backends can emit or accept. The protocol is transport‑agnostic, working over SSE, WebSockets, webhooks or any custom channel. A reference HTTP implementation and default connector let teams bootstrap an integration in minutes. Its middleware layer provides loose event format matching, enabling interoperability across diverse agent frameworks and UI stacks.
keyFeatures: Standard event schema: Defines about sixteen interoperable event types for agent‑to‑UI communication.
Transport agnostic: Works with SSE, WebSockets, webhooks or custom transports without code changes.
Bi‑directional state sync: Keeps UI state and agent context synchronized in real time.
Generative UI messages: Supports structured and UI‑rich payloads that can render dynamic components.
Middleware layer: Performs loose format matching and compatibility adaptation across frameworks.

useCases.title: In‑app AI assistants
useCases.description: Developers embed conversational agents directly into web or mobile apps, using AG‑UI to stream chat and UI updates without building custom protocols.

useCases.title: Customer support chatbots
useCases.description: Support teams deploy AI‑driven bots that exchange events with the support UI, enabling real‑time context enrichment and handoff to human agents.

useCases.title: Tool‑augmented IDE extensions
useCases.description: IDE plugins use AG‑UI to synchronize code suggestions, tool usage, and user actions, providing a seamless human‑in‑the‑loop experience.

useCases.title: Real‑time data dashboards with AI insights
useCases.description: Analytics dashboards integrate agents that push streaming insights and UI widgets, keeping visualizations in sync with live data.

useCases.title: Multi‑agent collaboration tools
useCases.description: Platforms that coordinate several agents leverage AG‑UI to share state and events across agents and the collaborative UI layer.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers and AI engineers building interactive agent‑powered applications. Requires familiarity with TypeScript/JavaScript and event‑driven architectures. Ideal for teams that need a lightweight, cross‑framework contract for real‑time agent communication.
